accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE National Curriculum in England, mathematics Year 3 measurement ('know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year and leap year'). Month lengths checked against the Gregorian calendar (HM Nautical Almanac Office / Royal Museums Greenwich leap year explainer): 30 days in April, June, September, November; February 28, or 29 in a leap year; the other seven 31; 365 and 366 days; years divisible by 4 are leap years except century years not divisible by 400 (2000 yes, 2100 no), which the adult text states. The lab only uses 2024–2035, where 'every 4 years' is exact. Knuckle mapping checked month by month (July and August both on knuckles). Parameterised answers 60*n, 60+s, 60*m and s-60 stay positive whole numbers at every corner (s from 65).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented slips from NCETM Year 3 measures guidance and the Nuffield/ATM work on time: a minute treated as 100 seconds (stopping past 60 gives '1 minute is 60 seconds, not 100', and 1 minute 30 seconds as 130 is named), alternating 30/31 all year (the July→August jump on the knuckles, prediction '30' for August, challenge tag alt), September given 31 (sort feedback quotes the rhyme), every even year or every year ending in 0 being a leap year (leap-year taps on 2026 and 2030, tags even and zero), the leap day placed in December (mastery m4, tag dec), and 365 vs 366 confusion (build step, tag norm).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmonths is about calendar units only: a second-hand dial that the learner must stop at exactly 60, 90 and 120 seconds, two drawn fists where each month must go on the next knuckle or dip, a drag-to-box month sorter by day count, a 2024–2035 year grid for leap years, and a year bar that sums all 12 months to 365 and then 366 with 29 February. It differs from flagcal (week and year wheels, hopping days), the 60-minutes/24-hours lesson and the clock-reading labs; the gate reports under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each fact is found in the lab before the text states it: the learner sees one full turn equals 60 and must convert 1 minute 30 seconds by stopping at 90; the knuckle order itself produces 31/30 and forces the July–August knuckle pair; sorting six months fixes the four 30-day months; tapping years shows the 4-year rhythm and that 2026 and 2030 are not leap years; and adding all 12 months shows where 365 comes from and that the one extra day makes 366.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 100 seconds in a minute (the hand turns once at 60), August 30 days after July 31 (August lands on a knuckle), December or August having 30 days (both sort into 31), every year or every 10 years for leap years (the grid shows 2024, 2028, 2032) and 360 or 366 days in a normal year (the bar stops at 365). The task completion message echoes the locked-in choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each, every one with its own message: hundred (a minute is 60 not 100), one (60 seconds is only 1 minute), sep (the rhyme), feb (only February has 28), apr and dec (only February can have 29; December is a knuckle month), norm and big (a leap year adds just one day), zero and even (ending in 0 or being even does not make a leap year; count in 4s), alt (July and August are both knuckles) and feb2. In-lab wrong moves also name the slip, e.g. 'Knuckles and dips take turns. After a knuckle comes a dip.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits (kid text short sentences, FK within the 6.5 limit; adult within 9.5). Canvas prompts are one short instruction ('Stop the hand at 1 minute 30 seconds.', 'Where does March go? Tap the next knuckle or dip.'), and the curriculum words used are the precise ones for the age: second, minute, month, leap year, 365 and 366 days.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each step has one job (seconds, knuckle order, month lengths, leap years, year total) and every feedback line carries a number or a rule. Item explanations give the reason (60 + 30, count on in 4s, the rhyme) rather than restating the prompt.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark, before and after Show me on every step. After the first pass the knuckle labels were split (knuckle months above, dip months below) so names no longer overlap the circles, February shows 28 in its dot with the leap-year note in the banner, and the challenge canvas now shows the completed fists instead of empty hands. Year and month tiles are 3 per row on phones, about 40 px tall, and every canvas action is repeated by full-size buttons below.

accessibility.evidence: Everything works with buttons: '+10 seconds', 'Stop: that's it', 'Next knuckle'/'Next dip', the three day-count boxes, one button per year and per month, and 'Make it a leap year'. After every move the canvas aria-label states the state, e.g. 'Goal: 1 minute 30 seconds. The hand shows 70 seconds.' or 'Next month: August. Knuckle or dip?'. Challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.
